source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Casts case retrieval as a policy in a memory-augmented MDP. The retrieval policy is a softmax over learned Q-values (soft Q-learning). The LLM stays frozen. This is the direct RL form of CASCADE-style value-based case choice.
numbers: Policy pi(c|s,M)=exp(Q/alpha)/sum exp(Q/alpha); TD update of Q on (state, case, reward). Parametric Q is a 2-layer MLP over SimCSE embeddings; non-parametric variant is cosine similarity only.
limits: Q is learned from a binary success reward (recast as a CE loss: Q = P(case is a good reference)). Reward is sparse and noisy for deep-research tasks.
agent_relevance: Template for a scaffold that scores stored cases by outcome, not only by similarity.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Learned (parametric) Q retrieval beats similarity-only retrieval, but only by a small margin, and both beat no memory over five learning iterations on DeepResearcher.
numbers: Table 4 (avg score, iter1 to iter5): no CBR 78.65 to 84.47; similarity CBR 79.84 to 84.85; learned-Q CBR 80.46 to 85.44. Learned-Q minus similarity: +0.62, +0.97, +1.01, +0.81, +0.59 points. Learned-Q minus no memory: +1.81 at iter1, +0.97 at iter5.
limits: Gap between learned and similarity retrieval is under 1.1 points. No confidence intervals or seeds reported. The gain over no-memory also shrinks with iterations.
agent_relevance: Value learning adds a small, early gain. Do not expect large gains from a learned retrieval score over plain similarity.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Number of retrieved cases: a few help, more does not. Performance peaks at K=4 and then plateaus or dips.
numbers: Table 3 DeepResearcher avg F1/PM: K=0 59.9/72.2; K=1 63.6/77.9; K=2 63.7/78.1; K=4 64.5/78.5; K=8 64.1/78.2; K=16 63.9/78.1; K=32 63.9/78.1. The first case gives +3.7 F1 and +5.7 PM; every later case adds under 1 point.
quote: CBR benefits from a small, high-quality memory, unlike few-shot prompting
limits: Planner gpt-4.1, executor o4-mini. Differences between K=1 and K=32 are under 1 point, likely noise.
agent_relevance: Retrieve one to four cases. The first retrieved case carries nearly all the benefit, so top-1 selection quality matters most.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Case memory gives consistent additive gains on top of planning, but size depends on the benchmark. Out-of-distribution gains are 4.7 to 9.6 points.
numbers: Ablation (F1/PM): CBR adds HLE +4.5/+7.0, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2. OOD sets (MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA) with 4 cases from NQ/TQ/HotpotQA/2Wiki trajectories: +4.7 to +9.6 absolute. GAIA val 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%. GAIA avg pass@1 70.91% with gpt-4.1 planner vs 63.03% with o3 planner.
limits: Authors say CBR cannot add domain knowledge that is missing (HLE). Data contamination noted on DeepResearcher (offline to online executor drop of 18.0 F1). Single runs.
agent_relevance: Case memory helps most where tasks share structure; it cannot supply missing knowledge.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Two-phase retrieval: first recall candidates by semantic similarity (k1), then re-rank by a blend of similarity and a learned Q-value (k2 injected). Q is updated with a Monte Carlo style rule from the environment reward for items actually shown in context. LLM frozen.
numbers: Memory triplet = (Intent, Experience, Utility Q). Blend weight lambda swept over {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}. HLE retrieval sizes (k1,k2): sparse 3/1, moderate 5/3, dense 10/5.
limits: Reward is task success; for HLE this means repeated exposure to the same questions (see c10).
agent_relevance: Closest published match to a bandit over cases: explore by similarity, exploit by learned value, blended.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Learned-utility retrieval beats similarity-only baselines and other memory systems over 10 runtime epochs.
numbers: Table 1 avg Last-epoch/Cumulative success: No memory 0.631; RAG 0.679/0.699; Self-RAG 0.673/0.726; Mem0 0.681/0.712; MemP 0.736/0.760; MemRL 0.772/0.798. MemRL minus MemP: +3.6 last-epoch, +3.8 CSR. MemRL last/CSR: BigCodeBench 0.595/0.627, OS 0.788/0.804, DB 0.960/0.972, ALFWorld 0.949/0.981, HLE 0.570/0.606. Backbones differ per benchmark (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5-mini, Gemini-3-pro).
limits: Backbone differs per benchmark. Single run per cell, no error bars reported. Cumulative success counts a task solved if solved in any epoch, which flatters methods that explore.
agent_relevance: A learned value on stored experiences gave +3.6 points over the best heuristic memory and +9.3 over plain RAG (last-epoch average).

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Blend ablation: the Q-weight has an inverted-U curve. Pure similarity (lambda=0) plateaus; pure Q (lambda=1) is volatile and loses context fit.
numbers: Best at lambda=0.5 (Figure 5; numeric values are only in the figure). Text: lambda=0 cannot filter functional distractors; lambda near 1 gives volatility and context detachment.
limits: Exact numbers not in text. Sweep shown for one task family.
agent_relevance: Keep a similarity term in the score. A pure value-based choice drifts from the task. A mixed score is the safe default.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Learned Q-values track true usefulness: strong correlation with empirical success, and some failure memories keep high Q (useful near-misses).
numbers: Pearson r=0.861 between Q and success rate; success rises from 21.5% (lowest Q bin) to 88.1% (highest). About 12% of memories in the 0.9-1.0 Q bin are failure trajectories.
limits: Correlation measured on the same runs that trained Q. Not a held-out calibration test.
agent_relevance: A value score can be audited by binning it against outcomes. Cheap test for our scaffold.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Transfer with the memory frozen after training, and ablation against single-task reflection (Reflexion-like).
numbers: Frozen memory on held-out sets: MemRL beats MemP by +2.8 points average (ALFWorld +5.8, OS +2.6). Cross-task retrieval beats single-task feedback by +9.0 on OS and +5.1 on ALFWorld; on HLE single-task 0.610 vs MemRL 0.606 (tie).
limits: HLE tie shows no benefit from cross-task retrieval there. Gains largest for multi-step tasks (ALFWorld +6.2 pp CSR), smaller for single-turn (BigCodeBench +2.5).
agent_relevance: Value-based case choice pays most on repeated procedural tasks; on diverse knowledge questions it does not beat per-task feedback.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Boundary condition: gain depends on task repetition. The HLE gain is runtime memorisation, not transfer.
numbers: Intra-dataset similarity vs gain: ALFWorld sim 0.518, gain +0.172 (max); HLE sim 0.186 but gain 0.357 to 0.570 (+0.213), explained by repeated exposure to the same questions over epochs. Retrieval size: moderate (5/3) beat dense (10/5) on the HLE CS/AI subset.
limits: The HLE number partly reflects seeing the same test items again across epochs, so it is not clean generalisation.
agent_relevance: Report held-out results separately from in-run results when scoring our own case selection.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Are Semi-Parametric Reinforcement Learning Agents (REMEMBERER)
finding: Early LLM-agent version of value-tagged case memory. Each record holds (goal, observation, action, Q estimate). Q is updated with an n-step bootstrapped rule (RLEM). Retrieved records show the highest-Q actions as encouraged and low-Q ones as discouraged. LLM frozen.
numbers: WebShop (2-shot) avg score/success: LLM-only 0.55/0.29; ReAct 0.66/0.36; REMEMBERER 0.68/0.39; RL 0.55/0.18; IL 0.60/0.29; IL+RL 0.62/0.29. WikiHow avg reward/success: LLM-only 2.58/0.90; Mobile-Env 2.50/0.89; REMEMBERER 2.63/0.93. Training: 10 tasks, 74 steps vs about 100k steps for RL/IL.
limits: Gains over ReAct are +0.02 score and +3 points success on WebShop and +0.05 reward on WikiHow. Small. No significance test.
agent_relevance: Value-tagged cases cost little to train and beat RL/IL baselines in sample efficiency, but the lift over a good fixed exemplar is small.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Are Semi-Parametric Reinforcement Learning Agents (REMEMBERER)
finding: Ablations on WikiHow: removing the discouraged-action advice and removing observation similarity both hurt; removing task similarity does not; bootstrapping matters for value accuracy.
numbers: Avg reward WikiHow: full 2.63; w/o bootstrapping 2.54; w/o random advice 2.64; w/o discouraged actions 2.48; w/o task similarity 2.63; w/o observation similarity 2.47. Reward-estimate error with bootstrapping 0.12 on WikiHow and 0.02 on WebShop.
limits: Discouraged and similarity ablations only on WikiHow (budget). WebShop shows no visible bootstrapping effect (0.67 vs 0.66). Success-rate columns were garbled in the PDF text, so only reward is reported.
agent_relevance: Negative (low-value) cases are useful, not only winners. Similarity on the current observation matters more than on task text.

source: Zhang, Feng, Tan (2022) Active Example Selection for In-Context Learning
finding: First Q-learning treatment of choosing in-context examples as a sequential decision. Shows example choice causes huge variance, and a learned policy helps small models but the benefit fades in larger ones.
numbers: GPT-2: 12.1% improvement over a max-entropy active-learning baseline on a seen task; 5.8% average improvement on unseen tasks. Random 4-shot sets differ by over 30 points on some tasks; worst sets fall below chance on TREC (10.0% vs 16.7% chance). Best reordering gives +8.1% over random sets. Gain diminishes for GPT-3 Babbage and Curie; small gain on Ada.
limits: Old models (GPT-2, GPT-3 Ada/Babbage/Curie), classification only. Policies learned on GPT-2 transfer weakly to bigger models.
agent_relevance: As models get stronger, learned example choice matters less. Expect smaller wins on current frontier models.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: Supervised stand-in for learned case value: score each candidate by the LM probability of the correct output when it is the prompt; train a dense retriever on top-k positives and bottom-k negatives (contrastive). Beats BM25 and SBERT similarity.
numbers: With GPT-Neo as scorer and inferer, best baseline to EPR: BREAK 26% to 31.9%; MTOP 57% to 64.2%; SMCalFlow 51.4% to 54.3%. Similar gains with GPT-Neo as proxy for GPT-J, GPT-3, Codex.
limits: Needs labeled training outputs and a scoring pass per candidate (cost). Semantic-parsing tasks, where copying structure from the prompt works well.
agent_relevance: Utility measured by outcome likelihood is a better retrieval target than surface similarity. Offline form of the bandit reward.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Learning to Retrieve In-Context Examples for Large Language Models (LLM-R)
finding: Distils LLM feedback into a reward model (cross-encoder), then trains a dense retriever; two training iterations. Generalises to held-out tasks and other LLMs.
numbers: Average +7.8% over random selection on 30 tasks with LLaMA-7B. Held-out 4 tasks avg: zero-shot 62.0; random 75.5; BM25 75.4; E5-base 76.3; SBERT 75.3; LLM-R 81.7 (+5.4 over E5). Second iteration +0.8 on main average; later iterations no gain. Removing the reward model costs 0.8 points.
limits: Some held-out tasks share a category with training tasks. Retriever is a trained model, not an online bandit.
agent_relevance: Learned retrieval value transfers across tasks, with diminishing returns after about two rounds of refinement.

source: Yan et al. (2026) Memory-R1: Enhancing LLM Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
finding: RL (PPO and GRPO) trains a Memory Manager (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP) and an Answer Agent that filters retrieved memories (memory distillation). Outcome reward only; 152 training QA pairs.
numbers: LLaMA-3.1-8B GRPO vs Mem0: relative +28% F1, +34% BLEU-1, +30% LLM-judge on LoCoMo. Distillation ablation (F1/BLEU-1/J): PPO 39.3/30.9/57.4 to 41.0/32.9/57.5; GRPO 41.0/34.4/60.1 to 45.0/37.5/62.7.
limits: Trains model weights (not scaffold-only). Dialogue memory QA, not problem solving. Agent filters about 60 retrieved memories.
agent_relevance: Recall wide, then select narrow: a second selection stage on top of similarity helps.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Memory of distilled strategies from successes and failures, retrieved by plain embedding similarity (authors keep retrieval simple on purpose). Retrieving more items hurts.
numbers: WebArena overall success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points over no memory for three backbones; up to 20% relative gain and 16% fewer steps. WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 39.0; 1 retrieved item 49.7; falls as more are added (44.4 at 4 items).
limits: Intermediate values garbled in PDF text. Success/failure labels come from the LLM itself (self-judged), a reward-noise source. No learned retrieval value used.
agent_relevance: Even without a learned value, one well-chosen item beats many. The limit on K is a reason to learn which item to show.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
finding: Compares retrieval policies for procedural memory on TravelPlanner: random sample vs query-keyed vs average-key-fact (AveFact). Semantic retrieval helps only a little over random.
numbers: Commonsense score TravelPlanner: GPT-4o no memory 71.93, random 74.59, Key=Query 73.38, AveFact 76.02; Claude-3.5-sonnet 63.49 / 63.99 / 64.93 / 65.76; Qwen2.5-72b 56.57 / 59.76 / 61.71 / 63.41. Reflexion-style update was best (+0.7 over second-best, 14 fewer steps).
limits: Random sampling was above Key=Query for GPT-4o. Single runs. AveFact over random is +1.4 to +3.7 points.
agent_relevance: Similarity-only retrieval is a weak bar. Random cases from a good bank capture much of the benefit, so a learned value has a modest ceiling.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Ablation of how successful trajectories are chosen in ALFWorld: task-similarity kNN (Faiss) vs reasoning-step similarity vs random.
numbers: ALFWorld success: ReAct 40.0; random trajectories 42.5; reason-similarity 48.5; task-similarity (ExpeL) 59.0. HotpotQA: ReAct 28.0; hand-crafted insights 32.0; ExpeL 39.0.
limits: Selection is by similarity only (no value). Standard errors about 0.3 to 2.1 points. Small samples.
agent_relevance: Random case choice adds almost nothing (+2.5); relevance-based choice adds +19. Selection quality is where the lift is.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Hand-tuned memory scoring in an LLM agent: score = recency + relevance + importance (all alpha=1, min-max scaled; importance is an LLM rating). Not learned. Ablating memory, planning and reflection lowers believability.
numbers: TrueSkill believability: full 29.89 (sigma 0.72); no reflection 26.88; no reflection/planning 25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory/planning/reflection 21.21. Cohen's d = 8.16 full vs fully ablated. Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4)=150.29, p<0.001; 100 evaluators.
limits: Ablation removes memory entirely, so it does not test the score weights. Weights fixed at 1 with no tuning shown.
agent_relevance: The standard fixed-weight score is a baseline; learned weights (MemRL lambda) have not been compared against it directly.

source: Shi et al. (2024) Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification (TRIPLE)
finding: Treats choosing a prompt from a pool under a fixed evaluation budget as fixed-budget best-arm identification (successive halving, continuous rejects), with embedding clustering or function approximation. Beats UCB, uniform and NeuralUCB.
numbers: Large pool (150 candidates, budget 100): TRIPLE-CLST/GSE beat BO-EI by 21%/28% (GPT-3.5) and 31%/42% (Llama2), and NeuralUCB by 38%/45% (GPT-3.5) and 26%/16% (Llama2). At 10 evaluations per prompt: +9.7%, +13.5%, +17.4% over uniform (CR, CLST, GSE); about 8% at 20 per prompt.
limits: Prompts, not cases; Instruction-Induction and BigBench tasks. Gains fade as budget grows.
agent_relevance: When feedback is costly, successive-halving style elimination beats plain UCB. Fits a small budget of case trials.

source: Lin et al. (2024) Use Your INSTINCT: Instruction Optimization using Neural Bandits Coupled with Transformers
finding: NeuralUCB over frozen LLM hidden representations to pick instructions for ChatGPT. Explores uncertain instructions and exploits predicted-good ones.
numbers: Instruction induction: best accuracy on 11 of 20 shown tasks, average rank 1.8, better than APE, InstructZero and EvoPrompt; 3 seeds. Also improves the zero-shot chain-of-thought instruction.
limits: Black-box prompt search, not case retrieval. Needs a white-box model (Vicuna-13B) for the surrogate.
agent_relevance: A contextual bandit over text candidates works at small budgets (about 100 to 200 queries).

source: Ye et al. (2023) Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning (CEIL)
finding: Selects the whole exemplar set jointly with a determinantal point process, trained with contrastive feedback from the LM. Learned selection beats similarity-only and independent learned retrieval (EPR). Generation tasks gain most.
numbers: 12 datasets, 7 tasks. Over 20 points absolute gain on NLI tasks (QNLI, MNLI) vs learning-free baselines; up to 45% absolute over RANDOM retriever on a generation task; about 2% (Template split) and 5% (Standard split) over EPR on GeoQuery.
limits: Small, older LMs. Needs training data and LM scoring.
agent_relevance: Choose a set that is relevant and mutually diverse, not top-k independently.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows from past successes and retrieves them. A comparison point for relevance-only selection with no per-case value.
numbers: Relative success +24.6% (Mind2Web step-wise, cross-task) and +51.1% (WebArena) over baselines; gap up to 22.5 points on WebArena; gains of 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as the train-test gap widens.
limits: Successful trajectories only; no value estimate or negative cases. Different baselines per benchmark. Abstract and intro read, not every table.
agent_relevance: Curated successes alone lift results; a value score would be an add-on.

source: Synthesis across opened LLM memory studies (c02, c06, c14, c15)
finding: Three kinds of case selection are in use. (1) similarity only (ExpeL, ReasoningBank, AWM, Memp); (2) fixed weighted score (Generative Agents); (3) learned value or utility (Memento, MemRL, REMEMBERER, EPR, LLM-R, CEIL, Memory-R1). Learned value beats similarity in every direct test found, but the margin is small online (Memento under 1.1 points; MemRL +3.6 over MemP) and larger when trained offline with labeled data (EPR, LLM-R, CEIL).
numbers: Memento learned vs similarity +0.6 to +1.0 (c02); MemRL +3.6 over MemP last-epoch average (c06); EPR +2.9 to +7.2 over best baseline (c14); LLM-R +5.4 on held-out (c15).
limits: No study found runs a true multi-armed bandit with confidence bounds over cases for a frozen frontier LLM and reports regret. None compares Thompson sampling or UCB against greedy Q. Explore-exploit schedule and the cost of showing a bad case are untested.
agent_relevance: Open question for us: does explicit exploration (UCB, Thompson) beat greedy Q on a small case bank? No evidence either way.

source: Gap note: classical CASCADE and case-based RL (1990s)
finding: Not opened. The source row names CASCADE; the original CBR-plus-reinforcement papers from the 1990s and 2000s were not reachable this session because search quota was used up and the arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned HTTP 429.
limits: Unverified. Do not cite numbers from classical systems until another angle opens them.
agent_relevance: Treat the pre-2020 bandit/RL-CBR literature as a gap to fill in angles A and B.

source: Gap note: dedicated bandit tests for LLM case or demo selection
finding: Not opened. Searches for papers using UCB or Thompson sampling to pick few-shot demos or agent cases could not be run (search quota exhausted). Related opened work: TRIPLE (prompt pool), INSTINCT (instructions), Active Example Selection (Q-learning).
limits: A literature gap, not evidence of absence.
agent_relevance: Re-run the search when quota refills.
